identity.title: Hot swollen joint with effusion and painful/limited range of motion (refusal to bear weight)

technique.how: Expose and compare both joints: inspect for swelling and erythema, palpate for warmth and an effusion (patellar tap or bulge sign at the knee, fullness at other joints), then move the joint passively through its range. Note pain with small passive movements, restriction, and whether the patient will bear weight on the limb.
technique.prerequisites: Adequate exposure of both sides; assess before analgesia blunts findings when feasible.
technique.contraindications: Do not force range of motion in a suspected fracture or unstable prosthesis.

interpretation.positive_finding: An acutely painful, swollen, warm joint with effusion and painful limited passive motion is the expected picture of septic arthritis (joint pain sensitivity 0.85, joint swelling 0.78, fever 0.57) and mandates arthrocentesis before antibiotics.
interpretation.negative_finding: No exam finding rules out septic arthritis; fever is absent in over 40% of cases, and specificity of these findings against gout, pseudogout or reactive arthritis is low.
interpretation.pitfalls: Cellulitis over a joint, crystal arthritis and hemarthrosis look identical; pain on passive motion favors joint involvement over cellulitis. Elderly, immunosuppressed and prosthetic-joint patients may have muted findings.
interpretation.changes_what: A hot swollen joint with painful passive motion should trigger urgent aspiration (cell count, crystals, Gram stain, culture) and orthopedic review; do not treat as cellulitis.

estimates.target_condition: Nongonococcal bacterial (septic) arthritis - finding: joint pain
estimates.population: Adults presenting with an acutely painful and/or swollen joint (14 studies, 6242 patients, 653 with septic arthritis)
estimates.reference_standard: Gold standard for septic arthritis (positive synovial fluid or blood culture / clinical criteria as defined by included studies)
estimates.quote: Joint pain (sensitivity, 85%; 95% confidence interval [CI], 78%-90%), a history of joint swelling (sensitivity, 78%; 95% CI, 71%-85%)

sources.citation: Margaretten ME, Kohlwes J, Moore D, Bent S. Does this adult patient have septic arthritis? JAMA. 2007;297(13):1478-1488.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Never use absence of fever or a modest exam to exclude septic arthritis; prosthetic joints and immunosuppressed patients need aspiration on suspicion alone.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Hot swollen joint with fever, rigors, sepsis physiology, IV drug use or a prosthesis requires same-day aspiration and orthopedic/ID involvement; delayed treatment destroys the joint.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: Precision of effusion and warmth assessment is not reported in the RCE abstract; effusion detection is examiner-dependent, especially at the hip and shoulder.

extraction_notes: Only sensitivities are available from the Margaretten 2007 RCE abstract (PMID 17405973; JAMA not OA, tables not accessible), for joint pain, history of joint swelling and fever; specificities and LRs for effusion, warmth or painful range of motion are not in the abstract, so those fields are null and the record is partially_quantified. Pooled prevalence in the review cohort would be 653/6242 (0.105) but is left null because it is a study mix, not a clinical prevalence. Diagnostic power in the RCE lies in synovial WBC/PMN, which is off-bedside.
